project_1_short: Storage, Processing, and Transmission of Information on Millions of Shipments.
project_1_long: A high-load backend that stores and processes over 3 million different shipments. It is used by everyone from managers to regular employees, who have varying levels of access rights. Data is retrieved, updated, and modified not only by warehouse staff but also via the Ozon API. Webhooks have been created for the CodeReader service, which allows for quick and convenient barcode scanning.
project_2_short: A ready-to-use service for learning English through movies and TV shows on YouTube, along with various games to increase engagement.
project_2_long: Writing new features, fixing bugs, and deploying updates to the server for an English-learning service based on YouTube videos. The following features were implemented: multithreaded video processing, transcription handling, and various games designed to make our service more appealing to customers.
project_3_short: A simple service for viewing video content.
project_3_long: A personal project for viewing various video content. The frontend is built with Svelte 5, which communicates with the FastAPI backend via a REST API. It features a user system, video playback history tracking, and a search engine. All videos are stored in S3 in a special format that allows content to be delivered to thousands of users simultaneously. I created this format using automated workers that convert the source video with FFmpeg, transcoding it into various resolutions (360, 720, 1080) and a modern codec. The website features a video player built from scratch that automatically analyzes user data to select the optimal video quality.

project_4_long: A high-load backend that stores and processes over million different shipments. After consulting with our clients from China, we selected the best logistics solution for them for shipments between China and Russia.
project_5_short: Automatic analysis and processing of purchase bonuses
project_5_long: An automated script that uses the AmoCRM API to collect data on customers past and recent purchases, and assigns bonuses and discount tiers to loyal customers
project_6_title: Telegram bot for sellers on Wildberries
project_6_short: All kinds of analytics and calculators
project_6_long: It allows you to track various metrics, receive notifications when testing changes to various variables in the product card, and work with the Wildberries API. It also encrypts user data, such as API keys, for security.
project_7_title: Schedule Bot for Telegram, VK, and MAX
project_7_short: Multi-platform bot that helps students find their college schedule and notifies them when it changes.
project_7_long: Developed a multi-platform schedule bot for Telegram, VK, and MAX. Implemented automatic analysis of the college website, collection of all data, and its further processing. Users can quickly find their college schedule and receive notifications about schedule changes. Implemented a unified database layer for all messengers, a queue-based system for broadcasts and alerts, and concurrent request handling.

hash_hero_description: Instant client-side calculation of cryptographic hashes, non-cryptographic hash table keys, and integrity checksums. Supports SHA-2, SHA-3, Keccak-256, BLAKE2b/s, xxHash, MurmurHash2/3, CRC-32/64, Adler-32, Whirlpool, and GOST Streebog. No data leaves your machine.
hash_algo_sha256_desc: The primary cryptographic hash for SSL/TLS certificates, Git commits, and Bitcoin mining. Delivers the ideal trade-off between performance and collision resistance.
hash_algo_sha512_desc: Outputs a 512-bit digest (128 hex chars). Optimized for 64-bit CPU architectures, frequently running faster than SHA-256 while offering maximum post-quantum security margin.
hash_algo_sha384_desc: Truncated version of SHA-512 with a unique initial vector. Commonly required in high-compliance US Federal/Suite B cipher suites and TLS 1.3.
hash_algo_md5_desc: Lightweight 128-bit checksum. Cryptographically broken with instant collision vulnerabilities; suitable only for basic non-adversarial file integrity checks.
hash_algo_sha1_desc: A 160-bit digest formerly standard in Git and older TLS. Broken via collision attacks (SHAttered, 2017). Avoid in new cryptographic protocols.
hash_algo_keccak256_desc: The raw Keccak-256 specification with 0x01 padding. The core hashing algorithm of the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM), Solidity contracts, and address derivation.
hash_algo_sha3_256_desc: Standardized by NIST with 0x06 domain padding. Built on Keccak sponge construction, making it completely immune to length extension attacks.
hash_algo_sha3_512_desc: The highest-security SHA-3 variant. Well-suited for cryptographic research and long-term data security against quantum brute-force vectors.
hash_algo_sha3_384_desc: Intermediate 384-bit SHA-3 digest, structurally matched with 192-bit and 256-bit symmetric encryption standards.
hash_algo_sha3_224_desc: Compact SHA-3 digest engineered to replace legacy 224-bit hashes like SHA-224.
hash_algo_blake2b_desc: 64-bit optimized hash faster than MD5 and SHA-1 while matching SHA-3 security. Extensively utilized in WireGuard VPN, Argon2, and IPFS.
hash_algo_blake2b_256_desc: BLAKE2b configured to produce a compact 256-bit digest, providing high throughput on 64-bit systems with minimal digest length.
hash_algo_blake2s_desc: 32-bit architecture variant optimized for microcontrollers, embedded IoT hardware, and lightweight cryptographic operations.
hash_algo_xxhash32_desc: Extremely fast non-cryptographic hash algorithm executing near RAM speed limits. Provides outstanding avalanche effect and collision avoidance for in-memory indexing.
hash_algo_murmur3_128_desc: High-throughput 128-bit hash developed by Austin Appleby. Universally deployed in databases (Cassandra), Bloom filters, and large-scale data systems.
hash_algo_murmur3_32_desc: Standard 32-bit MurmurHash3. Ideal for in-memory hash maps, cache key distribution, and quick data bucketing.
hash_algo_murmur2_64_desc: 64-bit MurmurHash2 variant optimized for 64-bit architectures, frequently leveraged in high-load server key distribution.
hash_algo_murmur2_32_desc: 32-bit MurmurHash2 algorithm widely found in legacy data frameworks, search engines, and real-time metrics pipelines.
hash_algo_crc32_desc: Cyclic Redundancy Check (32-bit). Specifically designed to detect accidental transmission or storage errors in network packets (Ethernet), ZIP archives, and PNG images.
hash_algo_crc64_desc: 64-bit Cyclic Redundancy Check providing a substantially lower accidental collision probability for big file validation and storage blocks.
hash_algo_adler32_desc: Rolling checksum invented by Mark Adler. Computes faster than CRC-32 in pure software and is the core checksum standard in zlib compression.
hash_algo_streebog256_desc: Russian cryptographic hash standard (GOST R 34.11-2012, 256-bit). Developed by TC 26 using an AES-like substitution-permutation network (SPN).
hash_algo_streebog512_desc: 512-bit variant of GOST R 34.11-2012 (Streebog). Standardized for national digital signature verification and official cryptographic documents.
hash_algo_whirlpool_desc: 512-bit hash function designed by Vincent Rijmen and Paulo Barreto. Employs a heavily modified AES cipher square matrix (MDS matrix) for diffusion.
hash_algo_ripemd160_desc: 160-bit European cryptographic standard. Essential to Bitcoin address generation where it is combined with SHA-256 (HASH160).
hash_guide_intro: Hash functions map arbitrary amounts of data to fixed-size outputs. They are categorized into cryptographic hashes (irreversible, collision-resistant), fast non-cryptographic hashes (optimized for hash table lookups and Bloom filters), and cyclic checksums (designed for error detection in transmission).
hash_faq_q1: What is the difference between Keccak-256 and SHA3-256?
hash_faq_a1: Although Keccak won the NIST hash competition to become SHA-3, NIST changed the domain separation padding byte from 0x01 to 0x06 in the final standard. Ethereum launched prior to this update and kept the original Keccak-256. Consequently, their hashes for the same text do not match.
hash_faq_q2: What is the difference between cryptographic and non-cryptographic hashes?
hash_faq_a2: Cryptographic hashes (SHA-256, BLAKE2, Streebog) are designed to be mathematically irreversible and collision-resistant against malicious attackers. Non-cryptographic hashes (xxHash, MurmurHash) prioritize raw throughput for hash tables and Bloom filters, making them fast but vulnerable to intentional collision attacks.
hash_faq_q3: Can a cryptographic hash be decrypted or reversed?
hash_faq_a3: No. A hash is a one-way digest, not symmetric or asymmetric encryption. Information is irreversibly reduced. However, predictable or short inputs can be matched using precomputed rainbow tables or dictionary attacks.
hash_faq_q4: Which hash function should I use for user passwords?
hash_faq_a4: Never use raw fast hashes like SHA-256, SHA-512, or MD5 alone for passwords. Modern GPUs calculate billions of hashes per second. Always employ memory-hard key derivation functions such as Argon2id, bcrypt, or scrypt.
hash_faq_q5: When should I choose CRC32 or Adler-32 instead of SHA-256?
hash_faq_a5: CRC-32 and Adler-32 are error-detecting checksums, not secure hashes. Use them when you need to verify network packet integrity, compressed archives (ZIP/zlib), or stream transfer errors with minimal CPU overhead.
hash_faq_a6: xxHash is an exceptionally fast non-cryptographic algorithm that operates at the maximum bandwidth limits of system RAM while achieving near-perfect randomness. It is the gold standard for in-memory indexing, game engines, and databases.
hash_faq_a7: Streebog is the national cryptographic hash function of the Russian Federation. It replaced the outdated GOST R 34.11-94 and uses an internal structure based on the AES/Kuznyechik SPN design.
hash_faq_q8: Why does BLAKE2b have both 256-bit and 512-bit versions?
hash_faq_a8: BLAKE2b is naturally optimized for 64-bit processors using 64-bit words, internally computing a 512-bit state. It can be safely truncated to 256 bits, offering 64-bit speed while producing a smaller digest.
hash_faq_q9: Are my strings or files uploaded to your server?
hash_faq_a9: No. All computations are performed locally in your browser using WebAssembly and Web Crypto API modules. No data is transmitted across the internet.
hash_faq_a10: The avalanche effect is a fundamental property where a modification of a single bit in the input causes approximately 50% of the bits in the resulting hash to flip randomly.
